<reason>Both sides argued crisply, kept the clash narrow, and answered pressure with labelled A1/A2. PRO built a clean central mechanism (the encounter must happen where under-25s already are; the marginal pound buys redundancy in a channel nobody under 25 can find) and landed a genuinely good hit by showing CON's answer to Q1 drifted into "trailers on platforms that drive to a door the broadcaster owns," i.e. conceding that discovery is feed-led. CON, however, extracted more damage from PRO's own words. PRO's Q1 answer ("the destination already exists — iPlayer, the Mediatheken, already paid for") gave CON the decisive turn: if the marginal pound never commissions anything for the 13–25 audience, the clip delivers the seventeen-year-old to a shelf built for her parents, and PRO's "you can always commission another hour" is exactly the pound in dispute. CON also converted PRO's strongest line (CBBC/KiKA hand children to the platforms at twelve "with nothing waiting") into an argument for building the thing that waits, and used PRO's concession that "some audience follows the face" to sustain the creator-rent objection. PRO never squarely answered CON's "clips of what?" — that creator/short-form work can be originated youth content rather than derivative marketing — which was the cheapest available repair and would have blunted CON's whole "marketing without product" frame. CON's interpretive stretch (treating owned apps as "channel expansion") is a real cost, and PRO flagged it well, but it was set up in CON's opening rather than smuggled in late, and CON preserved a coherent priority ordering (fund the product, market it with clips). CON's closing reversal of PRO's recoverability asymmetry was sharper than PRO's original framing, giving it the cleaner final reason to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's turn on PRO's own answer: PRO said the destination is "already paid for" and "you can always commission another hour," which CON converted into "the marginal pound *is* the hour" — so the successful clip delivers the target viewer to a static shelf commissioned for over-50s and she does not click twice. That reframed PRO's recoverable-error asymmetry into the unrecoverable one and PRO never repaired it.</best_rebuttal>
